voice_performance.performance_intent: An engineer telling you something precise, not a narrator selling you something. Level, unhurried in the vowels but never slow, and completely unsentimental about the numbers. The drama belongs to the picture and the cut; the voice's job is to be trusted.
voice_performance.energy_curve: Flat and close on the hook. Slight lift at 'here is the part nobody mentions'. Tightest and fastest through the two numbers. Then a hard drop into the silence beat, and the last line spoken quieter than everything before it.
voice_performance.pause_policy: One real pause only, before the closing line, so the silence beat lands as silence rather than as a gap. Elsewhere the sentence breaks do the work; no filler pauses between clauses.

provider_notes.piper: Piper has no SSML and no per-word emphasis. Emphasis is written into the sentence structure instead - short declaratives, fragments where a stress is wanted. Pauses are inserted as real silence in the audio between per-section renders, not as tags in the text.

sections.label: Hook
sections.text: Your headphones do not block that sound. They add one.
sections.speaker_directions: Flat, close, certain. No lift at the end of the second sentence - it is a statement, not a reveal.

delivery_cues.delivery_note: The whole video rests on the contradiction in these two sentences. Do not decorate it.

enhancement_cues.description: Black frame. A single cyan waveform pushes in from the top edge and keeps travelling downward - the world's noise heading somewhere. Nothing stops it.
The word BLOCK is struck through and replaced by ADD, in place, without moving.

sections.label: The easy half
sections.text: It listens to the world, flips the wave upside down, and plays it back. The two meet. Both disappear.
sections.speaker_directions: Brisk through the three verbs, then two short sentences delivered as facts, not as a magic trick.

delivery_cues.delivery_note: This is the part every other explainer stops at, so get through it cleanly and do not linger.

enhancement_cues.description: The cyan trace is joined by an amber trace that is its exact mirror. They slide together and flatten into a single hairline. This is the only time the canonical cancellation diagram appears.

sections.label: The turn
sections.text: That part is easy. Here is the part nobody mentions.
sections.speaker_directions: Slight lift on the second sentence - the only place in the video where the voice invites you in.

delivery_cues.delivery_note: The pivot of the script. Everything before was setup; everything after is the actual idea.

enhancement_cues.description: The flat hairline is wiped away and the frame reorganises: a microphone at the top of the vertical frame, an ear at the bottom, and the empty distance between them left deliberately unexplained for a beat.

sections.label: The deadline
sections.text: When the microphone hears the noise, the noise is already on its way to your eardrum. A few centimeters away. Microseconds out.
sections.speaker_directions: Even through the first sentence. The two fragments land separately, each one a fact being set down.

delivery_cues.delivery_note: 'Already' is the load-bearing word in the whole script.

enhancement_cues.description: A pulse leaves the microphone and races down the frame toward the ear. A microsecond counter starts in the margin and does not stop for the rest of the video.
The gap between microphone and ear is dimensioned like an engineering drawing: a few centimeters, and the time that distance actually buys.

sections.label: The numbers
sections.text: Be forty microseconds late, and the cancelling starts to fail. Miss by a hundred, and at one kilohertz you are a tenth of a wave wrong.
sections.speaker_directions: Fastest and tightest passage in the video. The numbers are not dramatised; the speed does that.

delivery_cues.delivery_note: No rising intonation on the numbers - they are measurements, not surprises.

enhancement_cues.description: 40 microseconds appears in monospace as a tolerance band around the amber trace. Then 100 microseconds, and the amber trace slips visibly out of register with the cyan one - the flat line breaks and audible-looking residue returns.

sections.label: The consequence
sections.text: That is why an engine disappears and the person next to you does not. Low sound is slow and wide. A voice is quick. There is no time.
sections.speaker_directions: Slowing across the three short sentences. 'There is no time' is the flattest line in the video.

delivery_cues.delivery_note: This answers the complaint the viewer already has, so let it land before the close.

enhancement_cues.description: A frequency axis running the full height of the frame. Cancellation floods up from the low end and stops dead below where speech lives. Everything above the line keeps moving.
The band that cancellation actually covers is labelled once, in monospace, against the axis.

sections.label: Landing
sections.text: Silence is not a wall. It is arriving on time.
sections.speaker_directions: Quieter than everything before it. A real pause before the line - the picture is already still.

delivery_cues.delivery_note: No call to action. The reframe is the ending.

enhancement_cues.description: Everything stops. The grid holds still for the only time in the video, one flat hairline across the centre, the microsecond counter frozen mid-count. The title appears once, small, and the frame does not move again.

grounding.s4: US 9,786,264 - anti-noise must be time-aligned with the arriving sound at the ear canal entry
grounding.s5: US 9,786,264 (40 microseconds or less, preferably 25); Hacker News - 100 microseconds is 10 percent of one 1 kHz cycle
grounding.s6: SoundGuys - active cancellation covers roughly 50 Hz to 2 kHz; speech sits largely above it

metadata.timing_note: Section boundaries are measured from the rendered Piper audio (voice en_US-ryan-high, length_scale 1.06), not estimated. Video runs 41.5s: 0.25s lead-in, 40.17s of narration timeline, 1.13s of held silence after the last word.
